newsitem.title: USA: Compaq recalls AC adapters for notebook.
newsitem.headline: Compaq recalls AC adapters for notebook.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. Thursday began a voluntary worldwide recall on certain defective AC adapters supplied with its Armada 4100 notebook computers.
The adapters, which were also shipped as options or spare parts to resellers, may have defective connector pins and could pose an electrical shock hazard, Compaq said.
The adapters also came with docking stations, which allow the notebook computers to function like desktop computers.
The Armada 4100 computer itself is not affected by the recall.
The adapters included with the Armada 4100 family of products were sold worldwide from Sept. 23 through Nov. 20.
Only AC adapters with both part number 217984-001 on the bar code label, and three hollow connector pins in the recessed male connector on the power adapter are affected.
The recall will have no material financial impact on the Houston-based company, Compaq said.
Compaq, which reported the possible hazard to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, said it identified the potential problem through its own internal manufacturing testing processes.
The company has not received any customer reports of injury caused by the AC adapters, and the voluntary recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
Compaq is the fifth-largest computer company in the world and the largest global supplier of personal computers.
Its stock rose $2.125 to $83.875 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
